findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and will raise TypeError when instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with just `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members: `counter_names` (abstract property), `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. None of them are implemented here, so the class remains abstract and `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`. Previously the handler had a concrete `evaluate` returning `[]` and was safely instantiable. This turns a no-op into an unhandled exception in `process_detectors`. Either keep a concrete stub implementation or don't register the abstract class as `detector_handler`.

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) can raise ValueError for condition results outside PriorityLevel
findings.body: `new_status` is derived from `condition.evaluate_value(value)` results via `max(new_status, evaluation)`, and `DataCondition.condition_result` is user/DB-provided data, so it is not guaranteed to be one of the `PriorityLevel` members (25/50/75). `PriorityLevel(new_status)` will raise `ValueError: <n> is not a valid PriorityLevel` for any other non-zero value (e.g. a condition result of `1` or `True`), crashing detector evaluation for the whole data packet rather than skipping/logging. Consider validating the value or coercing to the nearest valid priority before constructing `PriorityLevel`.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still describes a list return value
findings.body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the signature and implementation now return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. Update the wording so implementers of the abstract handler aren't misled about the contract.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests can't detect a wrong value passed to the hook
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses its `value` argument, and the tests exploit this by passing values that don't match the data packet (e.g. `test_state_results_multi_group` builds the expected occurrence for `group_2` with `6` while the packet has `10`; `test_results_on_change`/`TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` pass `6` while the evaluated values are 100 and 10). As a result, a regression where `evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the wrong `value` (or the wrong group key's value) to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` would not be caught. Incorporate `value` (and `group_key`) into the generated occurrence so equality assertions actually verify the arguments.
